Subject: Outage learning digest & customer action playbook

Hi Rajesh / Megan,

Thanks again for your patience as our teams closed out the investigation. Attached is a concise customer-facing summary with a timeline and concrete verification steps we recommend for Arcadia Financial to validate that the issue will not recur. Highlights below — the PDF and CSV include the full technical appendix.

Summary (short version):
- What happened: During a rolling model rollout we observed a KV-cache eviction bug that caused a small percentage of in-flight requests to receive corrupted KV-state, resulting in truncated responses and tokenization inconsistencies for ~14 minutes on 2028-02-24 21:12 UTC.
- Impact: ~0.8% of requests for the affected model experienced degraded output quality; no customer data was exfiltrated and no authentication or authorization controls were impacted.
- Root cause: a race condition in the KV cache eviction path combined with an unusual token length distribution for Arcadia's workload that exposed a GPU memory reclamation edge case.
- Immediate mitigations applied: emergency rollback to the previous stable model build; hotfix deployed to patch the cache eviction ordering; temporary rate smoothing applied for high-concurrency routes.
- Next steps (what Redwood will do): ship the cache-ordering fix to all regions, add an automated regression test that reproduces Arcadia's token distribution, and provide a verification playbook + runbook for your SREs.

Requested customer actions (short):
1) Run the attached verification_playbook.docx against a small sample of production traffic (instructions included).
2) Confirm results by EOD 2028-02-28 so we can mark the incident as closed for your account.
3) If you want, schedule a joint verification call; we suggest a 30-minute slot to step through the playbook with your engineers.

Attachments: arcadia_postmortem_summary_v1.pdf (RCA + timeline), incident_timeline_20280225.csv (raw events), verification_playbook.docx (stepwise checks + test harness).

If you have immediate compliance/attestation needs (SOC2 evidence, audit logs), let me know and I will loop in our Trust team and provide the relevant artifacts.

Respectfully,
Soojin Lee

Hi Rajesh, Soojin — looping in a couple folks with implementation context. Answers inline below.

On Sat, Feb 25, 2028 at 10:02 AM Rajesh Patel <r.patel@arcadiafin.com> wrote:
> 1) Can you confirm whether the rollback purged any cached customer session state or whether that state was preserved?

We preserved session-level metadata (session IDs, auth tokens) across the rollback. The affected KV cache entries were ephemeral inference state (model KV cache for attention contexts) and were regenerated on first request after rollback. That caused a transient extra-tail latency for a small number of requests but did not require user-side resync.

> 2) Could you send a short artifact showing the exact process that triggered the eviction?

Attached to Soojin's earlier email is the incident_timeline_20280225.csv. High level cause: an order-of-operations regression during the rolling deploy where cache eviction ran on worker threads before the worker had finished migrating in-flight caches. Under normal token distributions this was masked; Arcadia's workload had a higher-than-average median token window which increased likelihood of the race. We've reproduced this in our test harness and added a new pre-deploy gate.

Additional notes (technical):
- Fix shipped today corrects the eviction ordering and adds a barrier that prevents reclamation until in-flight caches are quiesced.
- We also instrumented an early-warning metric (kv_eviction_races) and will alert prior to rollback-required states.

Action items we will own (timeline):
- 2028-02-25 (complete): hotfix and automated test added to CI.
- 2028-02-27 (in progress): rollout of the fix to EU and APAC with verification.
- 2028-03-05: automated regression gate added to the model rollout pipeline; we will share the test code.

Hannah Schmitt
VP, Production Engineering
Redwood Inference
